**New York**, often called **New York City** (**NYC**),[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-10) is the [most populous city in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population "List of United States cities by population"). It is located at the southern tip of [New York State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State "New York State") on [New York Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Harbor "New York Harbor"), one of the world's largest natural harbors. The city comprises [five boroughs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_boroughs "Five boroughs")—[Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens "Queens"), [the Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx "The Bronx"), and [Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island "Staten Island")—each being coextensive with [its respective county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_New_York "List of counties in New York"). It is the geographical and demographic center of both the [Northeast megalopolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeast_megalopolis "Northeast megalopolis") and the [New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area "New York metropolitan area"), the largest metropolitan area in the United States by both population and urban area. New York is a [global center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_center "Global center") of [technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_technology "High technology"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCLargestTechTalentHubWorld-11)[finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_center "Financial center")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCFinancialCapitalWorldA-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCFinancialCapitalWorldGFCI-13) and [commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_New_York_City "Economy of New York City"), [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_New_York_City "Culture of New York City"), [entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Entertainment_Capital_of_the_World "The Entertainment Capital of the World") and [media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_in_New_York_City "Media in New York City"), academics and [scientific output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_scientific_output "List of cities by scientific output"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCScientificCapital-14)[the arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_arts "The arts") and [fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_capital "Fashion capital")—and as home to the [headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations "Headquarters of the United Nations") of the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), international [diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy "Diplomacy").[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-20) New York City is known for its fast pace and continuous urban energy.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-FastPaceNYC1-21)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-FastPaceNYC2-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-FastPaceNYC3-23)

With an estimated population of 8,584,629 in July 2025,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCQuickFacts-5) distributed over 300.46 square miles (778.2 km 2), New York is the [most densely populated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population_density "List of United States cities by population density") major city in the United States. New York City has more than double the population of [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), the country's second-most populous city.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-CensusNYC-24) More than 20.1 million people live in New York City's [metropolitan statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-25) and over 23.5 million people live in its [combined statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_statistical_area "Combined statistical area") as of 2020; both are the largest in the U.S. New York City is one of the world's most populous [megacities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megacities "Megacities").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-26) The city and its metropolitan area serve as the premier gateway for legal [immigration to the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_the_United_States "Immigration to the United States"). An estimated 800 languages are spoken in New York City,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCWorld'sMostCulturallyLinguisticallyDiverseCityTop-27)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCWorld'sMostLinguisticallyDiverseCity3Top-28)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-QueensMostLinguisticallyDiverseTop-29) making it the most linguistically diverse city in the world.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCWorld'sMostLinguisticallyDiverseCity1-30)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCWorld'sMostLinguisticallyDiverseCity2-31) The New York City metropolitan region is home to the [largest foreign-born population of any metropolitan region in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_born#Metropolitan_and_urban_regions_with_the_largest_foreign-born_populations "Foreign born"), numbering approximately 5.9 million people as of 2023.

[Manhattan Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Island "Manhattan Island") was [inhabited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenapehoking "Lenapehoking") by [Munsee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munsee_language "Munsee language")-speaking [Lenape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenape "Lenape") around 1624. By then, [Dutch colonists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_colonization_of_the_Americas "Dutch colonization of the Americas") had established [Fort Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Amsterdam "Fort Amsterdam") as a center of trade on the island. This was the first European settlement in what would become New York City. The settlement was named [New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Amsterdam "New Amsterdam") in 1626 and was [chartered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter "Charter") as a city in 1653. The city came under [English control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_colonization_of_the_Americas "British colonization of the Americas") in 1664 and was temporarily renamed New York after [Charles II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Charles_II_of_England "King Charles II of England") granted the lands to his brother, the [Duke of York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_II_of_England "James II of England"),[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-npsnetherland-32) before this name was permanently adopted in 1674. Following independence from the [Kingdom of Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain"), the city was the [national capital of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_capitals_in_the_United_States "List of capitals in the United States") from 1785 until 1790.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-senate-33) The modern city was formed by the [1898 consolidation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidation_of_New_York_City "Consolidation of New York City") of its five boroughs.

Anchored by [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street") in Manhattan's [Financial District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_District,_Manhattan "Financial District, Manhattan"), New York City has been called both the world's premier financial and [fintech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fintech "Fintech") center[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCFinancialAndFintechCapitalWorld-34)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-reuters-2022-03-24-35) and the most economically powerful city in the world.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NewYorkMostPowerfulGlobalCity-36)As of 2024[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_York_City&action=edit), the New York metropolitan area is the [largest metropolitan economy in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_GDP "List of cities by GDP"), with a [gross metropolitan product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._metropolitan_areas_by_GDP "List of U.S. metropolitan areas by GDP") of over US$2.44 trillion.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-37) The New York metropolitan area's economy is [larger than all but nine countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal) "List of countries by GDP (nominal)"). Despite having [a 24/7 rapid transit system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Subway "New York City Subway"), New York also leads the world in urban automobile [traffic congestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_congestion "Traffic congestion").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCCongestion-38) The city is home to the world's two [largest stock exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largest_stock_exchanges "Largest stock exchanges") by [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization "Market capitalization") of their listed companies: the [New York Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange "New York Stock Exchange") and [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq"). New York City is an established haven for global investors.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCSafeHavenGlobalInvestors-39)

As of 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_York_City&action=edit), New York City is the most expensive city in the world for [expatriates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expatriate "Expatriate")[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-MostExpensiveCityExpats-40) and has the highest residential rent costs of any American city;[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCMostExpensiveRents-41)[New York County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_County "New York County") (Manhattan) is by a significant margin the most expensive [U.S. county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._county "U.S. county") in terms of average home price per square foot[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-ManhattanHighestMedianPricePerSquareFoot-42) and produces the [highest U.S. county GDP by both absolute and per capita measures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._counties_by_GDP "List of U.S. counties by GDP"). [Fifth Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Avenue "Fifth Avenue") is an ultra-luxury international shopping corridor that is undergoing additional infrastructure investment.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-FifthAvenueUltraLuxuryInvestment-43) Amidst escalating [affordability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordability "Affordability") concerns,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCCostOfLiving-44) New York City is home to the [highest number of billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_number_of_billionaires "List of cities by number of billionaires"),[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCHighestNumberBillionaires-45) individuals of [ultra-high net worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_net_worth_individual "High net worth individual") (greater than US$30 million),[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NYCUltraHighNetWorth-46) and [millionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_number_of_millionaires "List of cities by number of millionaires") of any city in the world by a significant margin.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-NewYorkArtMarketGlobalHeadquarters-47)

## Etymology

See also: [Nicknames of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicknames_of_New_York_City "Nicknames of New York City")

In 1664, New York was named in honor of the Duke of York (later King [James II of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_II_of_England "James II of England")).[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-48) James's elder brother, [Charles II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_England "Charles II of England"), appointed him [proprietor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proprietary_colony "Proprietary colony") of the former territory of [New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Netherland "New Netherland"), including the city of [New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Amsterdam "New Amsterdam"), when England [seized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquest_of_New_Netherland "Conquest of New Netherland") it from [Dutch control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_colonization_of_the_Americas "Dutch colonization of the Americas").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Archdeacon2013a-49) New Netherland was renamed the [Province of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_New_York "Province of New York") (now [New York State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State "New York State")).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-50)

## History

Main articles: [History of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City "History of New York City") and [Timeline of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_New_York_City "Timeline of New York City")

Further information: [History of Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Manhattan "History of Manhattan"), [Timeline of Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Brooklyn "Timeline of Brooklyn"), [Timeline of Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Queens "Timeline of Queens"), [Timeline of the Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_Bronx "Timeline of the Bronx"), and [Timeline of Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Staten_Island "Timeline of Staten Island")

### Early history

Main article: [History of New York City (prehistory–1664)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City_(prehistory%E2%80%931664) "History of New York City (prehistory–1664)")

In the [pre-Columbian era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Columbian_era "Pre-Columbian era"), the area of present-day New York City was inhabited by [Algonquians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquian_peoples "Algonquian peoples"), including [Munsee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munsee_language "Munsee language")-speaking [Lenape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenape "Lenape").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-51) The homeland of the Lenape, known as [Lenapehoking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenapehoking "Lenapehoking"), included the present-day areas of [Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island "Staten Island"), [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), [the Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx "The Bronx"), the western portion of [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island") (including [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn") and [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens "Queens")), and the [Lower Hudson Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Hudson_Valley "Lower Hudson Valley").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-52)

The first documented visit to [New York Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Harbor "New York Harbor") by a European was in 1524, by [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_people "Italian people") explorer [Giovanni da Verrazzano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_da_Verrazzano "Giovanni da Verrazzano").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Debo2013-53) He claimed the area for [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_France "Kingdom of France") and named it _Nouvelle Angoulême_ (New [Angoulême](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angoul%C3%AAme "Angoulême")).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-rodgers-54) A Spanish expedition, led by the Portuguese captain [Estêvão Gomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%AAv%C3%A3o_Gomes "Estêvão Gomes") sailing for [Emperor Charles V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor"), arrived in New York Harbor in January 1525 and charted the mouth of the [Hudson River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River"), which he named _Río de San Antonio_ ('Saint Anthony's River').[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-55)

In 1609, the English explorer [Henry Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Hudson "Henry Hudson") rediscovered New York Harbor while searching for the [Northwest Passage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Passage "Northwest Passage") to the [Orient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orient "Orient") for the [Dutch East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_India_Company "Dutch East India Company").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Lankevich2002-56) He sailed up what the Dutch called [North River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_River_(Hudson_River) "North River (Hudson River)") (now the Hudson River), named first by Hudson as the _Mauritius_ after [Maurice, Prince of Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice,_Prince_of_Orange "Maurice, Prince of Orange").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-hudsonnni-57)

Hudson claimed the region for the Dutch East India Company. In 1614, the area between [Cape Cod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod "Cape Cod") and [Delaware Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware_Bay "Delaware Bay") was claimed by the Netherlands and named _Nieuw-Nederland_ ("[New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Netherland "New Netherland")"). The first non–Native American inhabitant of what became New York City was [Juan Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_(Jan)_Rodriguez "Juan (Jan) Rodriguez"), a merchant from [Santo Domingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captaincy_General_of_Santo_Domingo "Captaincy General of Santo Domingo") who arrived in Manhattan during the winter of 1613–14, trapping for [pelts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelts "Pelts") and trading with the local population as a representative of the Dutch.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-58)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-59)

### Dutch rule

Main articles: [New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Amsterdam "New Amsterdam"), [Fort Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Amsterdam "Fort Amsterdam"), and [New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Netherland "New Netherland")

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Stad_Amsterdam_in_Nieuw_Nederland_%28City_Amsterdam_in_New_Netherland%29_Castello_Plan_1660.jpg/250px-Stad_Amsterdam_in_Nieuw_Nederland_%28City_Amsterdam_in_New_Netherland%29_Castello_Plan_1660.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stad_Amsterdam_in_Nieuw_Nederland_(City_Amsterdam_in_New_Netherland)_Castello_Plan_1660.jpg)

The [Castello Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castello_Plan "Castello Plan"), a 1660 map of [New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Amsterdam "New Amsterdam") in [Lower Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Manhattan "Lower Manhattan")

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/GezichtOpNieuwAmsterdam.jpg/250px-GezichtOpNieuwAmsterdam.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GezichtOpNieuwAmsterdam.jpg)

[New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Amsterdam "New Amsterdam"), centered in what eventually became Lower Manhattan, in 1664, the year [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_colonization_of_the_Americas "British colonization of the Americas") took control and renamed it New York

A permanent [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_colonization_of_the_Americas "European colonization of the Americas") presence near [New York Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Harbor "New York Harbor") was established in 1624, making New York the [12th-oldest continuously occupied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_North_American_settlements_by_year_of_foundation "List of North American settlements by year of foundation") European-established settlement in the [continental United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_United_States "Continental United States"), with the founding of a Dutch [fur trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fur_trading "Fur trading") settlement on [Governors Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Island "Governors Island"). In 1625, construction began on a [citadel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citadel "Citadel") and Fort Amsterdam, later called _Nieuw Amsterdam_ (New Amsterdam), on present-day Manhattan Island.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-60)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Tolerance-61)

The colony of New Amsterdam extended from the southern tip of Manhattan to modern-day [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street"), where a 12-foot (3.7 m) wooden [stockade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockade "Stockade") was built in 1653 to protect against Native American and English raids.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-62) In 1626 [Peter Minuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Minuit "Peter Minuit"), the director of New Netherland, as charged by the [Dutch West India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_West_India_Company "Dutch West India Company"), purchased the island of Manhattan from the _[Canarsie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canarsee "Canarsee")_, a small [Lenape band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenape "Lenape"),[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-63) for "the value of 60 [guilders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_guilder "Dutch guilder")"[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-64) (about $900 in 2018).[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-65) A frequently told but disproved legend claims that Manhattan was purchased for $24 worth of glass beads.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-66)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-67)

Following the purchase, New Amsterdam grew slowly.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-npsnetherland-32) To attract settlers, the Dutch instituted the [patroon system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patroon "Patroon") in 1628, whereby wealthy Dutchmen (_patroons_, or patrons) who brought 50 colonists to [New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Netherland "New Netherland") would be awarded land, local political autonomy, and rights to participate in the lucrative fur trade. This program had little success.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-locnetherland-68)

By the authority of a charter granted by the [Dutch States General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_States_General "Dutch States General") in June 1621, the Dutch West India Company established an exclusive monopoly over colonization and commerce in New Netherland. In 1639–1640, to bolster economic growth, it relinquished its fur trade monopoly, prompting a shift toward the production of food, timber, tobacco, and enslaved labor (particularly with the [Dutch West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_Antilles "Netherlands Antilles")).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-npsnetherland-32)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-nahcnetherland-69)

In 1647, [Peter Stuyvesant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Stuyvesant "Peter Stuyvesant") began his tenure as the last [director-general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_of_New_Netherland "Directors of New Netherland") of New Netherland. During his tenure, the population of New Netherland grew from 2,000 to 8,000.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-70)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-71) Stuyvesant has been credited with improving law and order; however, he also earned a reputation as a [despotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despotic "Despotic") leader. He instituted regulations on liquor sales, attempted to assert control over the [Dutch Reformed Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Reformed_Church "Dutch Reformed Church"), and blocked other religious groups from establishing houses of worship.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-nyhsstuyvesant-72)

### English rule

Main articles: [Province of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_New_York "Province of New York") and [History of New York City (1665–1783)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City_(1665%E2%80%931783) "History of New York City (1665–1783)")

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/The_fall_of_New_Amsterdam_cph.3g12217.jpg/250px-The_fall_of_New_Amsterdam_cph.3g12217.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_fall_of_New_Amsterdam_cph.3g12217.jpg)

_[The Fall of New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fall\_of\_New\_Amsterdam "The Fall of New Amsterdam")_, painting by [Jean Leon Gerome Ferris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Leon_Gerome_Ferris "Jean Leon Gerome Ferris"), depicting the [Conquest of New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquest_of_New_Netherland "Conquest of New Netherland")

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/A_view_of_Fort_George_with_the_city_of_New_York%2C_from_the_SW.jpg/250px-A_view_of_Fort_George_with_the_city_of_New_York%2C_from_the_SW.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_view_of_Fort_George_with_the_city_of_New_York,_from_the_SW.jpg)

[Fort George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Amsterdam "Fort Amsterdam") and New York with British warships, c.1731

In 1664, unable to summon any significant resistance, Stuyvesant surrendered New Amsterdam to English troops, led by Colonel [Richard Nicolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nicolls "Richard Nicolls"), without bloodshed.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-nyhsstuyvesant-72)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-nnistuyvesant-73) The terms of the surrender permitted Dutch residents to remain in the colony and allowed for religious freedom.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-lehrmanstuyvesant-74)

In 1667, during negotiations leading to the [Treaty of Breda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Breda_(1667) "Treaty of Breda (1667)") after the [Second Anglo-Dutch War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Anglo-Dutch_War "Second Anglo-Dutch War"), the victorious Dutch decided to keep the nascent plantation colony of what is now [Suriname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suriname "Suriname"), which they had gained from the English,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-75) and in return, the English kept New Amsterdam. The settlement was promptly renamed "New York" after the [Duke of York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_II_of_England "James II of England") (the future King James II and VII).[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-homberger400-76) The duke gave part of the colony to proprietors [George Carteret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Carteret "George Carteret") and [John Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Berkeley "John Berkeley").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-77)

On August 24, 1673, during the [Third Anglo-Dutch War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Anglo-Dutch_War "Third Anglo-Dutch War"), [Anthony Colve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Colve "Anthony Colve") of the Dutch navy [seized New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Raid_on_North_America "Dutch Raid on North America") at the behest of [Cornelis Evertsen the Youngest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelis_Evertsen_the_Youngest "Cornelis Evertsen the Youngest") and rechristened it "New Orange" after [William III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_III_of_England "William III of England"), the [Prince of Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_of_Orange "Prince of Orange").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Roper2017-78) In November 1674, the Dutch returned the island to England under the [Treaty of Westminster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Westminster_(1674) "Treaty of Westminster (1674)").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-79)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-80)

Several intertribal wars among the Native Americans and epidemics brought on by contact with the Europeans caused significant Lenape population losses between 1660 and 1670.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-81) By 1700, the Lenape population had diminished to 200.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-82) New York experienced several [yellow fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_fever "Yellow fever") epidemics in the 18th century, losing 10% of its population in 1702 alone.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-83)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-84)

In the early 18th century, New York grew in importance as a trading port within the [surrounding colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_New_York "Province of New York").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Foote2004-85) It became a center of [slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_colonial_United_States "Slavery in the colonial United States"), with 42% of households enslaving Africans by 1730.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-86) Most were [domestic slaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_slave "House slave"); others were hired out as labor. Slavery became integrally tied to New York's economy through the labor of slaves throughout the port, and the banking and shipping industries trading with the [American South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_South "American South"). During construction in [Foley Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foley_Square "Foley Square") in the 1990s, the [African Burying Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Burying_Ground "African Burying Ground") was discovered; the cemetery included 10,000 to 20,000 graves of colonial-era Africans, some enslaved and some free.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-AsanteMazama2005-87)

The 1735 trial and acquittal in Manhattan of [John Peter Zenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Peter_Zenger "John Peter Zenger"), who had been accused of [seditious libel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seditious_libel "Seditious libel") after criticizing [colonial governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_of_New_York "List of colonial governors of New York")[William Cosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Cosby "William Cosby"), helped to establish [freedom of the press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_the_press "Freedom of the press") in North America.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-zenger-88) In 1754, [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University") was founded.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-89)

### American Revolution

Further information: [American Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution "American Revolution")

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/BattleofLongisland.jpg/250px-BattleofLongisland.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BattleofLongisland.jpg)

The [Battle of Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Long_Island "Battle of Long Island"), one of the largest battles of the [American Revolutionary War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War "American Revolutionary War"), which took place in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn") on August 27, 1776

The [Stamp Act Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamp_Act_Congress "Stamp Act Congress") met in New York in October 1765, as the [Sons of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons_of_Liberty "Sons of Liberty") organization emerged in the city and there were skirmishes over the next ten years with British troops stationed there.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-BoyerClark2009-90) The [Battle of Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Long_Island "Battle of Long Island"), the largest battle of the [American Revolutionary War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War "American Revolutionary War"), was fought in August 1776 within modern-day Brooklyn.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Reno2008-91) A British rout of the Continental Army at the [Battle of Fort Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Fort_Washington "Battle of Fort Washington") in November 1776 eliminated the last American stronghold in Manhattan, causing [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") and his forces to retreat across the Hudson River to [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), pursued by British forces.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-92)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-93)

After the battle, in which the Americans were defeated, the British made New York their military and political base of operations in North America.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-94) The city was a haven for [Loyalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loyalist_(American_Revolution) "Loyalist (American Revolution)") refugees and escaped slaves who joined the British lines for freedom promised by the [Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Crown "British Crown"), with as many as 10,000 escaped slaves crowded into the city during the British occupation, the largest such community on the continent.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-95)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-96) When the British forces [evacuated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evacuation_Day_(New_York) "Evacuation Day (New York)") New York at the close of the war in 1783, they transported thousands of [freedmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedmen "Freedmen") for resettlement in [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia"), England, and the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Hinks2007-97)

The attempt at a peaceful solution to the war took place at the [Conference House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_House "Conference House") on Staten Island between American delegates, including [Benjamin Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin "Benjamin Franklin"), and British general [Lord Howe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Howe,_1st_Earl_Howe "Richard Howe, 1st Earl Howe") on September 11, 1776.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-98) Shortly after the British occupation began, the [Great Fire of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Fire_of_New_York_(1776) "Great Fire of New York (1776)") destroyed nearly 500 buildings, about a quarter of the structures in the city, including [Trinity Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_Church_(New_York_City) "Trinity Church (New York City)").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-99)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-100)

### Post-revolutionary period and early 19th century

Main article: [History of New York City (1784–1854)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City_(1784%E2%80%931854) "History of New York City (1784–1854)")

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Ramon_Elorriaga_-_Inauguration_of_George_Washington.jpg/250px-Ramon_Elorriaga_-_Inauguration_of_George_Washington.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ramon_Elorriaga_-_Inauguration_of_George_Washington.jpg)

A portrait of the [first inauguration of George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_George_Washington "First inauguration of George Washington") in 1789

In January 1785, the assembly of the [Congress of the Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Confederation "Congress of the Confederation") made New York City the national capital.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-101) New York was the last capital of the United States under the [Articles of Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation") and the first under the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Post-Revolutionary_War-102) As the capital, New York City hosted the inauguration of the first President, [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington"), and the first [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress"), at [Federal Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Hall "Federal Hall") on [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street"). Congress drafted the [Bill of Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Bill_of_Rights "United States Bill of Rights") there.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Post-Revolutionary_War-102) The [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") held its first organizational sessions in New York in 1790.

In 1790, for the first time, New York City surpassed [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") as the nation's largest city. At the end of 1790, the capital of the United States was [moved to Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residence_Act "Residence Act"), where it remained while [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") was being constructed.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-residence_act-103)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-senate-33)

During the 19th century New York City's population grew from 60,000 to 3.43 million.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-104) Under New York State's [gradual emancipation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradual_emancipation "Gradual emancipation") act of 1799, children born to enslaved mothers were eventually liberated, but were legally required to serve as [indentured servants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indentured_servant "Indentured servant") until age 28 for males and age 25 for females.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-105)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-106) A significant free Black population gradually developed in Manhattan, made up of former slaves who had been freed by their masters after the [American Revolutionary War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War "American Revolutionary War"), as well as escaped slaves. The [New York Manumission Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Manumission_Society "New York Manumission Society") worked for abolition and established the [African Free School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Free_School "African Free School") to educate Black children.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Divided-107) It was not until 1827 that [slavery was completely abolished in the state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_slavery_in_New_York_(state) "History of slavery in New York (state)").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-108) Free Blacks struggled with discrimination, and interracial [abolitionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionist "Abolitionist") activism continued. New York City's population jumped from 123,706 in 1820 (10,886 of whom were Black and of whom 518 were enslaved) to 312,710 by 1840 (16,358 of whom were Black).[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Census1790to1990-109)

[![Image 32: A painting of a snowy city street with horse-drawn sleds and a 19th-century fire truck under blue sky](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Hippolyte_Sebron_-_Rue_De_New-York_En_1840.jpg/250px-Hippolyte_Sebron_-_Rue_De_New-York_En_1840.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hippolyte_Sebron_-_Rue_De_New-York_En_1840.jpg)

[Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_(Manhattan) "Broadway (Manhattan)"), which follows the Native American [Wecquaesgeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wecquaesgeek "Wecquaesgeek") Trail through Manhattan, 1840[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-110)

In the 19th century, the city was transformed by both commercial and residential development relating to its status as a national and international trading center, as well as by European immigration.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Rosenwaike-111):[55](https://archive.org/details/populationhistor00irar/page/55) The city adopted the [Commissioners' Plan of 1811](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioners'_Plan_of_1811 "Commissioners' Plan of 1811"), which expanded the city [street grid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_plan#Early_United_States_(17th%E2%80%9319th_centuries) "Grid plan") to encompass almost all of Manhattan. The 1825 completion of the [Erie Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erie_Canal "Erie Canal") through [central New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_New_York "Central New York") connected the [Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic "Atlantic") port to the agricultural markets and commodities of the North American interior via the Hudson River and the [Great Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Lakes "Great Lakes").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-112) Local politics became dominated by [Tammany Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tammany_Hall "Tammany Hall"), a [political machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_machine "Political machine") supported by [Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_diaspora "Irish diaspora") and [German immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_diaspora "German diaspora").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-113) In 1831, [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University") was founded.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-114)

Several prominent American literary figures lived in New York during the 1830s and 1840s, including [William Cullen Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Cullen_Bryant "William Cullen Bryant"), [Washington Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Irving "Washington Irving"), [Herman Melville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Melville "Herman Melville"), [Rufus Wilmot Griswold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_Wilmot_Griswold "Rufus Wilmot Griswold"), [John Keese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Keese "John Keese"), [Nathaniel Parker Willis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathaniel_Parker_Willis "Nathaniel Parker Willis"), and [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe "Edgar Allan Poe"). Members of the business elite lobbied for the establishment of [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), which opened in the winter of 1858 as the first [landscaped park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landscape_design "Landscape design") in an American city.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-115)

The [Great Irish Famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Irish_Famine "Great Irish Famine") brought a large influx of Irish immigrants, of whom more than 200,000 were living in New York by 1860, representing over a quarter of the city's population.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-116) Extensive immigration from the German provinces meant that Germans comprised another 25% of New York's population by 1860.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Harris-117)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-118)

### American Civil War

Main articles: [New York City in the American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_in_the_American_Civil_War "New York City in the American Civil War") and [History of New York City (1855–1897)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City_(1855%E2%80%931897) "History of New York City (1855–1897)")

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/The_Departure_of_the_7th_Regiment.jpg/250px-The_Departure_of_the_7th_Regiment.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Departure_of_the_7th_Regiment.jpg)

Departure of the [7th New York Militia Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7th_New_York_Militia_Regiment "7th New York Militia Regiment") for the defense of Washington, D.C., April 19, 1861

[Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") candidates were consistently elected to local office, increasing the city's ties to the South and its dominant party. In January 1861, in the wake of the [Southern secession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_secession "Southern secession"), New York City Mayor [Fernando Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Wood "Fernando Wood") proposed to the [Common Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Council "New York City Council") that the city secede from both the United States and the State of New York to become an independent "free city" that could maintain its lucrative cotton trade, but his proposal was not acted on.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Divided-107) Anger at new [military conscription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_conscription "Military conscription") laws during the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War") (1861–1865), which spared wealthier men who could afford to hire a substitute, led to the [Draft Riots of 1863](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_Riots_of_1863 "Draft Riots of 1863"), whose most visible participants were ethnic Irish working class.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Divided-107)

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/New_York_Draft_Riots_Harpers_colored_asylum.jpg/250px-New_York_Draft_Riots_Harpers_colored_asylum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:New_York_Draft_Riots_Harpers_colored_asylum.jpg)

The [Colored Orphan Asylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colored_Orphan_Asylum "Colored Orphan Asylum"), looted and burned during the [Draft Riots of 1863](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_Riots_of_1863 "Draft Riots of 1863")

The draft riots deteriorated into attacks on New York's elite, followed by attacks on Black New Yorkers after fierce competition for a decade between Irish immigrants and Black people for work. Rioters burned the [Colored Orphan Asylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colored_Orphan_Asylum "Colored Orphan Asylum") to the ground.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Harris-117) At least 120 people were killed.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-McPherson-119) Eleven Black men were [lynched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynching_in_the_United_States "Lynching in the United States") over five days, and the riots forced hundreds of Blacks to flee. The Black population in Manhattan fell below 10,000 by 1865. The White working class had established dominance.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Harris-117)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-McPherson-119) It was one of the worst incidents of [civil unrest in American history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_incidents_of_civil_unrest_in_the_United_States "List of incidents of civil unrest in the United States").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-120)

### Late 19th and early 20th century

Main articles: [History of New York City (1898–1945)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City_(1898%E2%80%931945) "History of New York City (1898–1945)") and [History of New York City (1946–1977)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City_(1946%E2%80%931977) "History of New York City (1946–1977)")

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Mulberry_Street_NYC_c1900_LOC_3g04637u_edit.jpg/250px-Mulberry_Street_NYC_c1900_LOC_3g04637u_edit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mulberry_Street_NYC_c1900_LOC_3g04637u_edit.jpg)

Manhattan's [Little Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Italy,_Manhattan "Little Italy, Manhattan")c.1900

In 1886, the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty"), a gift from France, was dedicated in New York Harbor. The statue welcomed 14 million immigrants as they arrived via [Ellis Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island "Ellis Island") by ship in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and is a symbol of the United States and American ideals of liberty and peace.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Statue_of_Liberty_UNESCO-121)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-122)

In 1898, the City of New York was formed with the [consolidation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Greater_New_York "City of Greater New York") of Brooklyn (until then a separate city), the County of New York (which then included parts of the Bronx), the County of Richmond, and the western portion of the County of Queens.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-123) The opening of the [New York City Subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Subway "New York City Subway") in 1904, first built as separate private systems, helped bind the consolidated city together.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Cudahy2004-124) In the early 20th century, the city became a world center for industry, commerce, and communication.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Blake2009-125)

In 1904, the [steamship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steamship "Steamship")_[General Slocum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General\_Slocum "General Slocum")_ caught fire in the [East River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_River "East River"), killing 1,021 people.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Sheard1998-126) In 1911, the [Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle_Shirtwaist_Factory_fire "Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire"), the city's worst industrial disaster, killed 146 garment workers and spurred the growth of the [International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Ladies'_Garment_Workers'_Union "International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union") and major improvements in building safety standards.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-cornell1-127)

[![Image 36: A man working on a steel girder high above a city skyline.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Old_timer_structural_worker2.jpg/250px-Old_timer_structural_worker2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Old_timer_structural_worker2.jpg)

A [construction worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Construction_worker "Construction worker") atop the [Empire State Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_State_Building "Empire State Building") during its construction in 1930. The [Chrysler Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Building "Chrysler Building") is visible to the right.

New York's non-White population was 36,620 in 1890.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Rosenwaike-111):Table 30 New York City was a major destination in the early 20th century for Blacks during the [Great Migration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American) "Great Migration (African American)") from the American South, and by 1916, New York City had the largest urban [African diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_diaspora "African diaspora") in North America.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-GatesHigginbotham2009-128) The [Harlem Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_Renaissance "Harlem Renaissance") of literary and [cultural life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_New_York_City "Culture of New York City") flourished during the era of [Prohibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-Roche2015-129) The larger economic boom generated the construction of skyscrapers competing in height.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-130)

New York City became the most populous [urbanized area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area#United_States "Urban area") in the world in the early 1920s, overtaking London. The metropolitan area surpassed 10 million in the early 1930s, becoming the first [megacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megacity "Megacity").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-:1-131) The [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") saw the election of reformer [Fiorello La Guardia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiorello_La_Guardia "Fiorello La Guardia") as mayor and the fall of Tammany Hall after eighty years of political dominance.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City#cite_note-132)

Returning [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") veterans created a post-war [economic boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_cycle "Business cycle") and the development of large [housing tracts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_tract "Housing tract") in eastern Queens and [Nassau County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nassau_County,_New_York "Nassau County, New York"), with Wall Street leading America's place as the world's dominant economic power. The [United Nations headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_headquarters "United Nations headquarters") was completed in 1952, solidifying New York's global [geopolitical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geopolitical "Geopolitical") influence, and the rise of [abstract expressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_expressionism "Abstract expressionism") in t
